glosses: To move (a word or clause) to the start of a sentence (or series of adjectives, etc).

examples.text: […] in the clause, only the adjective may be fronted; but if both a past participle and a verbal particle are present, either may be fronted. Topicalization, in which maximal projections are fronted to express pragmatics such as contrast, emphasis, ...
A problem facing any syntactic analysis of hyperbaton is that nonconstituent strings are fronted […] In cases where the adjective is fronted with the determiner, the determiner is not doubled […]

glosses: To act as a front (for); to cover (for).

examples.text: Everybody knew Skopas fronted for the fight mob even though he was officially the arena manager.

glosses: To lead or be the spokesperson of (a campaign, organisation etc.).

examples.text: Ray Winstone is fronting a campaign for the Football Association that aims to stop pushy parents shouting abuse at their children during the grassroots football season.

glosses: Of an alter in a person with multiplicity (especially in dissociative identity disorder): to be the currently actively presenting member of (a system), in control of the person's body.

examples.text: Fronting can be understood as a representation of who controls the system, that is, the person to whom you are speaking. Emilia was typically the person fronting her system.

glosses: To provide money or financial assistance in advance to.

examples.text: I'm prepared to say that I fronted you the money for a business deal with me, and the investment paid off brilliantly.

glosses: To assume false or disingenuous appearances.

examples.text: So when I tell people where I'm from and check their reactions, I know in my heart I'm just frontin’. Because the way and where I lived then pales when compared to the way and where many youths are living today.
What's with these homies dissin' my girl? / Why do they gotta front?

No matter how hard she fronted in the coming years, Carmiesha could never forget that she had given birth and had a child in this world. Even when she tried not to remember, she still couldn’t forget.
Boy don't try to front, / I-I know just-just what you are, are-are.
You know damned straight what this is about, or you ain't as smart as you been frontin'.

glosses: To deceive or attempt to deceive someone with false or disingenuous appearances (on).

examples.text: You think that you can front when revelation comes? / You can't front on that

glosses: To appear before.

glosses: Flexible, pliant, bendable.

examples.text: He's so limber that he can kiss his knee without bending it.

glosses: To cause to become limber; to make flexible or pliant.

examples.text: Her stiff hams, that have not been bent to a civility for ten years past, are now limbered into courtesies three deep at every word

glosses: A two-wheeled vehicle to which a wheeled artillery piece or caisson may be attached for transport.

examples.text: An' when the smoke 'ad cleared away, before the limber wheels, / There lay the Driver's Brother with 'is 'ead between 'is 'eels.
